title: How to Verify a TokenRate Price Estimate
description: See what the calculator includes, what it cannot infer from a token count, and how to reconcile it with your invoice.
tldr: TokenRate applies catalog text-token rates to the counts you enter. Verify the exact model and rate date, then add cache, batch, tools and other billable categories from your provider's usage report.

sections.heading: What the calculator computes
sections.body: [Tokens to USD](/tools/token-to-usd) multiplies the input and output counts you provide by the corresponding per-million-token catalog rates. In single-count mode it shows two separate estimates. In input-plus-output mode it adds the two costs. The formula is visible beside the calculator.

sections.heading: Where rates can differ
sections.body: Provider price sheets change. An aggregator route, model snapshot, service tier or long-context request can use another rate from a headline model entry. Always compare the exact model ID and route on your bill to the linked provider price sheet. The displayed catalog update date tells you when the data file changed, not when every provider last verified a particular SKU.

sections.heading: What a token count cannot reveal
sections.body: A pair of text token counts cannot identify cached reads, cache writes, batch discounts, image or audio units, tool calls, web search, storage, taxes or credits. It may also omit billable reasoning unless the provider reports it inside output usage. Those categories must come from the provider dashboard or invoice.

sections.heading: Reconcile one billing period
sections.body: Export model-level usage for a day or month. Apply the appropriate rate to each billing category, sum the line items, then compare with the invoice. Investigate large differences by checking retries, tier changes, cached tokens and alternative routes. If you see a stale or incorrect model rate on TokenRate, use the [contact page](/contact) with the model ID and official price link.

faq.question: Is a TokenRate result an invoice?
faq.answer: No. It is an estimate for standard text-token usage at the catalog rate shown; the provider invoice is authoritative.

ctaText: Estimate your own usage with TokenRate tools, then compare with the provider's billing page.
